title: Roy’s lifeline
text: We purchased the Komp subscription in 2020. Occasional teething problems and loss of connection from time to time but this has been a lifeline between my family and my father in his care home throughout lockdown. We still chat every day and he has been able to watch his great grandson develop from a newborn in 2020 to now. Little Henry has got to know dad this way where he might otherwise have been a stranger. Dad is now unable to walk so the family can come to him and send him photos of their lives. I don’t know what we would do without it. I can monitor dads moods and physical health and chat to his carers as they pop in with his tea etc. these things would be impossible on a normal phone call. I do wish I could post videos of Henry’s development but we watch them on my phone when I visit. There is a slight drawback in that he is immobile so the Komp must remain in exactly the right place to see him in his armchair. If the cleaner moves it by mistake I can’t see him fully. But we have guide tape on the floor and table to show where things need to be.  I’m amazed there are no other residents or indeed anyone I’ve met who has even heard of the Komp. I feel like an unofficial ambassador for the company as I tell people how wonderful it is whenever I meet someone who might benefit. Thank you so much. Diane Gittings.  From Kent and Sussex in the UK.

title: Window to the world
text:
Before we discovered the KOMP device, I had long wished that just such a thing would come along and thanks to No Isolation, my wish eventually became reality.
If you are an elderly, or disabled person for whom using a PC, laptop or notebook for communications is difficult and for whom a mere telephone cannot provide the pleasure of face-to-face contact with friends and family, then KOMP is the answer.
Supremely simple and fuss free to use (no technical knowledge or experience required), the KOMP allows you to enjoy chats with loved ones at any time you wish as well as the possibility of seeing their photographs and receiving text messages on screen.
All of this is done on a high quality stand alone screen (very similar to a smallish TV).
When friends call, as long as you have the unit switched on you will hear a countdown tone for 10 beats along wit the name of whoever of your invited friends (no strangers can call you) then you will see them and be able to talk to them as a video call.
It’s simple, reliable, trouble free and great fun and it’s the perfect answer for maintaining contact without the hassle of computers, mobiles and other such devices.
I had one for my bedbound mum-in-law and I also have one for my own mum. Both families are great fans of the KOMP and during the current crisis it became even more essential than normal. Will would never want to be without this device and I cannot recommend it highly enough!

title: Life changing & huge screen
text:
We sadly lost our Mum recently & Dad became too poorly to care at home so he now lives in a residential home, caring & lovely people but obviously missing life with us. It’s been a tough time. We all visit on a regular basis & on good days take him out…..He struggles with his phone so I wanted something easy & found Komp, all I can say is it’s made such a huge difference for several reasons. 1/ we can send messages & texts & viewing on a large screen makes a big difference 2/ We can video call so he can see us clearly, the sound is excellent too 3/ He called us from his phone one evening saying he was poorly so we got on the Komp to see & reassure him a nurse was on her way to him 4/ We send funny jokes too which brightens his day. We like that it just has 1 button, on, off & sound. I think all care homes could look at installing these into their living rooms for everyone to gain access 
🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟 So impressed & I must be as I never leave reviews. Thank you

title: Music Controls keep changing for the worse
text: Please give us the ability to assign our own music controls in the music control mode, or at the last, the option to revert to different formats. I've loved my Fossil Hybrid HR for the ~2y I've had it, but the several changes to music controls in recent months have continued to make it worse and worse for me. ... The middle button - which previously served both to pause (tap) and the return to home (hold) - was simplified to only performing the latter in all modes.  Not only does this lower the number of available quickly-accesses modes from 3 to 2, it also forces a remap of the 5 music control functions onto the remaining 4 input options, complicating the inputs mostly at the expense of the least used one (for the avg. customers): the rewind. ... While I'm surely an outlier, this was the watch's main function for me since I use it primarily for audiobook rewinds. Rewinds have gone from requiring taps (<1 sec); to requiring to holds (~1 sec); to requiring a hold to pause, holds to rewind, and a final hold to play again (>5 sec). Audiobook readers may require 1-10 presses per minute if a particular passage or line is difficult to understand. The feedback is also not instantaneous, so unlike before where I'll immediately hear the next words upon tapping/holding, I have to unpause to check where in the passage I am. What used to take <5 sec to input may take >20 now. This delay, along with the finicking with controls back and forth, disrupt my comprehension of I'm trying to understand, and so I probably end up taking 10x longer to get through difficult passages now. Simply put, it's not worth the effort and I just get my phone out now, so I don't use the smartwatch for anything but checking the time now. Fossil is great outside of this, but it does hurt to be in a niche group of customer that may be ignored.

text:
I do like the app for its appearance and usability, but the annoyance of the weather’s refresh overshadows the positive aspects. 

Every time I look at my watch (a Collider HR), the weather and chance of rain show two dashes, not synced. I have to go to my phone and open the app to get it to sync up. The app is configured to use precise location always, and it’s not closed, it’s running in the background. title: It’s nice that Apple has decided to set a default timer for you
text:
All in all, I like the Apple Watch but a few updates ago Apple decided to set a default timer of 15 minutes on the watch. This is new behavior as prior to this, when you went to the timer you simply selected the timer you wanted and you were good to go. 

Now however, Apple has decided that whenever you launch the timer they will set a default timer of 15 minutes for you. How do they know I want a 15 minute timer? Their support site says they chose 15 minutes as it is a good compromise between various activities like working out or other things. I’ve never used my timer during workouts. I use it when I’m grilling, or other things none of which ever requires a 15 minute timer. So now, every time I use the timer, I have to cancel the default 15 minute timer and set it to what I actually want. 

Here’s an idea for you Apple, don’t assume anything for your customers, let us decide what timer we want. Either get rid of the default timer (which never used to be a thing) or if you insist on being our big brother and make decisions for us, then let us set our own default timer setting in settings. I frankly don’t want a default timer set every time I assume the app, I simply want to quickly and easily set my own timer. Assuming you know what is best for everyone and make decisions for your customers is completely arrogant. Worthless.

title: Fall detection? I call BS.
text:
I have my watch for multiple reasons. One of those being fall detection because I am a professional equestrian rider. I have fallen no less than a dozen times since purchasing my first watch with “fall detection.”

Most recently I have an Apple Watch Series 9. I have come off of a horse 3 times (HARD) while having this watch and none of those  times was there an emergency alert. However, I have clapped my hands excitedly for someone and also had a mild roll off of my body ball while stretching where my watch has gone off. What gives on when this thing registers? Do I have to pound my fist on the ground (if I’m conscious) after I’ve come off to get a fall to register? WTH Apple?

I realize that an accelerometer is the primary source that registers to tell the watch to make an emergency call, but Apple really should rethink their “fall detection.” 

My mother had several falls as an elderly obese person that were not registered. This was the absolute primary reason for the purchase. We had backup emergency buttons as well. 

I’ve had numerous hard hits to the ground from horses or otherwise and there has been no “fall” detected. 

I am well aware that this is not the end all be all in fall detection, but it fails nine times out of 10 in actual fall scenarios versus false positives for ridiculous everyday movements. 

Come on Apple, I know you can do better. I am absolutely happy to be a test subject for your fall detection upgrades since I continue to have many  instances in which it SHOULD register. 

My only saving grace is that, THANKFULLY,  the times I have come off, my cellular has worked. That is also a very sketchy issue. Cellular on the Apple Watch works at its own convenience.

title: Eight Isn’t Enough
text: We set up Caring Village for my family of 8 siblings to help monitor and manage our parent’s health. This site has everything we need and is so simple to use on your laptop, iPad or phone. The journal feature allows each of us to capture with our visits or calls with our parents to share with the family current health issues or follow up from doctor’s appointments. It’s so much better than just texting each other. We also use the Calendar feature to track appointments so that one of us can join them in person or on a call to make sure we capture all the notes for reference. The ability to upload documents and maintain all the information on each of their various Drs makes it really easy for us to coordinate. Most importantly, the team at Caring Village, particularly Linda, has been amazingly responsive whenever we needed clarify a process or make suggestions for improvements. Caring Village has been absolutely perfect for our family to be actively engaged in our parents health.

title: This app carried me through one of the hardest seasons of my life
text:
I spent the last few years caring for my mom while she was living with stage 4 lung cancer. Nothing truly prepares you for how overwhelming caregiving becomes — emotionally, physically, and mentally. Every day felt like a juggling act: driving back and forth for chemotherapy, managing medications, updating advance medical directives, coordinating travel so she could see friends and family, scheduling physical therapy, managing oxygen equipment, dealing with insurance and deductibles, and trying to secure medical appointments months in advance.

It was exhausting. And often, it felt very lonely.

Caring Village brought calm and clarity into a situation that otherwise felt like constant chaos. The medication management section alone was a godsend — one less thing to keep in my head when I was already running on fumes. Having a shared calendar to coordinate tasks gave structure to days that felt overwhelming, and being able to communicate with the caregiver we hired in the later months — all in one place — made an enormous difference.

What mattered most was the peace of mind. Caring Village helped me feel supported, organized, and less alone at a time when everything felt heavy. It dramatically lowered my stress and allowed me to be more present with my mom, instead of constantly worrying about what I might be forgetting.

This app is clearly built by people who understand caregiving not as a checklist, but as a deeply human experience. I’m profoundly grateful it existed when I needed it most.

Thank you, Caring Village.

title: Bonnie S.
text:
I am a geriatric care manager and I discovered this app when I was trying to juggle communication among 30+ family members for one of my clients. I since have started several more “villages” for other clients and use most of the available options. Overall I love this app. I have the following observations to share in hopes it helps people make a decision about using this and also in hopes the developers are reading reviews

Pros: 
-ability to care plan and have staff document daily in the wellness journal to monitor compliance and communicate with family. 
-ability to message multiple people at once
-family and client ability to remain updated on status and keep all involved in the loop consistently 
-family ability to ask questions, send messages, add items to the calendar, etc. it promotes transparency among family, client and care team
-ability to use calendar to schedule staff and appointments. Also able to assign staff to tasks and ask for volunteer from family at times there is no staff in the home

Cons:
-friends can see most of what the inner circle sees. This poses a privacy issue for those not given authorization to see medical and clinical details. I have had to minimize information shared and can’t fully use the app in one of my cases
-inability to archive closed cases for future reference. They can only be deleted
-the care plan is only good for one day then disappears. From an agency perspective this limits our ability to do quality assurance and track trends
-notifications to email only link to the site but not the actual action it is notifying about so it takes extra time to locate what has been added
-inability to retract a message or edit
-support is quick to respond and helpful. However when I asked to whom I could direct my recommendations to I got no response. I’m hoping this review may get into the proper hands to address some of these suggestions for improvements 

Despite the “cons”,  have adopted used of this app for all of my clients receiving in-home care and feel it meets most of our needs.

title: Terrible Experience
text:
I have a Galaxy Watch Series 3 and it doesn’t work very well with iOS.

First off, the "find phone" function is next to useless - it plays a very quiet sound and the option on the watch almost always seems to be greyed out. Turns out it requires the Galaxy Watch app to be running in the background, which is almost never the case even though I have background app refresh enabled. It seems to rely on media volume rather than ringtone volume, and I usually keep the media volume low.

Secondly, I hate how Weather, Store, and other apps rely on having a constant connection to your phone even when their function could reasonably be done over WiFi. It wasn't like this before - I used to be able to use these apps on WiFi just fine. Now they demand a connection to my phone constantly.

Finally, while this isn't a problem with the app (as far as I know), the watch once randomly decided to reset itself. It just said "Watch will be reset" and just wiped itself with no indication as to what triggered the reset. I don't know why or how it did this. A web search only revealed other users confused by a similar problem. The only thing I could find was some guy claiming it happens if you press the power button a bunch of times, but I didn't press power (if I did, it's way too easy to accidentally trigger.)

The only thing that has been consistently reliable is notifications - I've never missed a notification with the watch connected.

title: Wonderful Service for Those Living Alone
text:
I am retired, live alone and have health issues, but am still able to care for myself. But I have nobody regularly checking on me. I am very busy, but my hobbies and pastimes tend to be done indoors, so neighbors are used to not seeing me outside for days at a stretch. Therefore, if I should ever fall or not be able to phone for help for any reason (Heaven forbid!), nobody would “miss me” for a long while. There are regular texts between me and several close relatives, but even they would not think anything was wrong if a week went by without hearing from me for a “catch-up.”
So - Enter SNUG!  What a wonderful service ( and the Basic Plan, which is all I need at present, is so helpful, easy-to-use, and FREE). I just set the alarm on my phone for a few
minutes before the daily check-on time I have given Snug. At this chosen time, I open my Snug App, check the box and immediately receive a cheery message on the same screen, saying I’m good for another day! 
And if I DON’T check the box within a few minutes, Snug notifies the back-up person I have provided, who will then check on me . 
So convenient, comforting and easy-peasy to use!

title: Suggested Improvements
text: This app has a useful concept, but the check-in system needs better logic. I’ve had multiple false alerts simply because my phone battery died or the device was turned off, which causes unnecessary notifications to my contacts. For an app focused on safety, that is a real issue, especially for anyone using the paid plan that may escalate to calls or authorities. The app should use passive signals like phone movement, background activity, charging events, or detecting a reboot to tell the difference between a missed check-in and an actual problem. A toggle for daily health tips instead of pithy quotes would also make the check-in screen more relevant. With these changes, the app would avoid many needless alerts.

title: It really works
text:
As a pet sitter and a single person I appreciate Snug having my back. I had gotten busy one evening and forgot to check in. Even though the app did its part by sending me text messages reminding me I had not yet checked in. I didn’t hear them. Within maybe 10 to 15 minutes later my phone was blowing up from my contacts making sure I was ok. It was an unintentional test of the system and it worked perfectly. All 5 contacts were notified and all did their part to make sure I was ok. 
Thank you Snug.

title: Life saving app.
text: I started using this app 3-4 months ago.  I had been looking for an app that would make me feel more secure as a middle-aged woman who lives alone.  There are times where I go days and weeks without speaking to a family member or friend.  I also work from home, and I have multiple pets.  The thought of me dropping dead for some random reason, and then my dogs subsequently starving to death, or whatever other ungodly things that take place when someone passes at home alone, etc…  But, now, I have this handy dandy app that I check in with every day.  And, if I don’t check in, my emergency contacts will get a text message from the app to inform them I’ve gone rogue.  I feel exponentially “safer” knowing I have this fail proof, back up system that ensures someone will be notified to come and check on my and my animals.  The app also sends multiple reminders so that you don’t forget to check in.  At any rate, I highly recommend this app.  It’s incredibly easy to use, and it gives me a peace of mind that I would not have otherwise.  Thanks, Snug!!!

title: Better Than A Phone Chain..and a real good idea.
text:
Help! I’ve fallen and can’t get up!

Oh my God, what will happen to me? No one knows. I live alone. What will my pets do? 

This is a real concern as people age. Wait, you’ll find out. I have. 

I used to have the Help I’ve fallen kit, and all the hardware and necklaces. And a big bill. 

I considered starting a phone chain and calling friends each day to check in. Intrusive. Cumbersome. Time consuming. 

So I found the SNUG app. Inexpensive. Add three trusted people. Check in once a day with SNUG by opening the app and hitting a button. 

Fail to, and SNUG will CALL YOU. Fail to answer SNUG will call your contacts and then 911 if it is a real emergency. 

A very useful app.

title: Love the APP
text:
UPDATE:I received the help I needed to get back into the app. While SNUG was in my contacts, the actual phone number was blocked. Not sure how that happened. Once unblocked I was able to receive the verification code and log back in.  Still the best and easiest app for single, elderly, disabled, college kids or similar to use and let family or friends know your safe without being intrusive. 

The app is simple and easy!! The reason I will NOT give it 5 stars is due to their customer service!!! If you ever get a new phone (same number) you need to re login and in order to do that you in put your number and wait for a code to enter. The problem is you will NEVER  get that code!!! So obviously the next step is to call but they will NEVER answer the phone and you have to leave a message. They will NEVER return your call. At this point the only way to check in is to call them and do the automated check in. Now you have to find their website   (Snugsafety.com…you’re welcome) and email support expressing your issue. At some point you’ll get a response with a code that lasts 10 mins or so, but since you aren’t attached to email that code will expire and not work. Do you see where I’m going with this? They have  lousy customer service!! It’s been this way since I’ve started using this app many years ago! I doubt they’ll ever make a change, but if you can suffer through those issues, the app itself is great! Still waiting for my code!!!!

title: Snug Safety Check-in Daily
text:
I have been using Snug since my new senior housing facility did not have much of an emergency 🆘, and inquired on Google for something to fit the bill so to speak.  I found this app on the Apple App Store and felt it would handle what I was concerned about.  ‘Let me tell you, it does’.  I one time forgot (in the beginning) to check in (I have the premium service @ $99/yr), and I have my brother listed as a Contact person.  They called him, he called me, they called me, would call 911 shortly if I didnt respond NOW!  My Time Limit was set at 12 Noon, I reported in at 12:02pm.  So, I now have changed from 00:01-11:59am to check in daily, to 00:01-13:30, or 12:01am to 1:30pm daily.  I now check in mostly mid mornings.  
It’s good to have, works in all of contiguous 48 states, where ever your cell phone is located.  BTW, age 84 and now a widower.

title: Mr Pete
text:
Snug is FANTASTIC app that I’m thrilled with. This is one of a very few app reviews I have ever written. I would rate it much higher if it were possible. I am using the free version which fits my needs perfectly.

Now I can no longer see my notes history, nor does the app have the Add Note or Edit Note features anymore! 

Why in the world would you eliminate such important features from this app?! I have literally been using this app and my Omron wrist cuff to get through a terribly frightening crisis, and I wake up today to the app that took away one of its most important features for my use of it! Now THAT will raise a patient’s BP even more! 

The app is useless if I have to document contextual notes elsewhere in another app (like a Notes app) per BP reading. It is stressful enough to be in the midst of medically trying to stabilize and regulate my BP again, and now I have lost the ease of documenting in-the-moment notes all in one place. 

As a software engineer myself, this change in usability is completely unacceptable for the user and renders the app essentially unusable for the purposes I have stated in this review. I cannot tell you how disappointed and upset I am at this removal of functionality!

title: New Update Makes Adding Notes Painfully Slow Since 8.5.0
text:
I’ve been using the Omron app for a long time, and the usability took a major step backward starting with version 8.5.0. The “New Home Screen” update introduced a workflow change that makes adding notes significantly more difficult than before.

Previously, I could add a note directly from the main screen. Now, when I tap a reading, the app takes about 10 seconds to load — and it always loads the chart first. I don’t need the chart, and I don’t use the chart for adding notes, yet I’m forced to see it every single time I want to annotate a reading. After that delay, I have to scroll down to “See all measurements,” but the scrolling is laggy and often requires several swipes before the app responds. Only after selecting “See all measurements” can I scroll again, enable “Show notes,” and finally add a note. This is a clear usability regression.

This change affected me during a medically sensitive moment. I was recently hospitalized for a stroke, and I rely on the ability to quickly annotate readings when symptoms or stress occur. The new slow, chart‑first workflow made it harder to document an important reading in real time, which is unacceptable for a health‑tracking app.

Omron should restore the ability to add notes directly from the main screen or streamline the workflow. Users who depend on this app for real medical situations should not be forced to wait through delays, laggy scrolling, and an unnecessary chart just to record essential information.

If this workflow cannot be improved, I may need to switch to another app that supports my Omron monitor, because quick note‑taking is essential for my medical tracking.

title: Absolutely love my Gear Fit2 Pro & this app but have questions
text:
**UPDATED**
My husband bought me the watch a few years ago.  In over 30 years of marriage definitely one of his best choices!  At that time I used the Android app on my LG K20 VS501; despite what many have reported I never experienced any problems even while using Bluetooth headphones.
The Android app allowed me to access music from my phone directly from the app while using the exercise tab for tracking walking.  Additionally, I was able to receive distance, speed, pace etc. cues audibly which I could set through my settings.  That feature was a big help!
Fast forward:  last summer I moved into the iPhone XR.  I set everything up with the Apple apps.  Connects easily every time, & this app also allows for easy syncing.  At first I drove myself crazy trying to find my 2 favorite features:  the music icon & audible cues.  At first I thought the cues were just not coming through my headset but after trying it without headphones I discovered there were none, only countdown.  (Countdown also does not come through Bluetooth headset.). I even switched to the running tab, thinking the option would be there; nothing.  Yes, I tried without music:  no more nice fellow voice to encourage me.
Although the missing link to my music can be worked around I really miss the audible cues.  Am I missing something as to how to find such setup ( which was easy in Android)?  Is there a reason why those features are not in the app for Apple?
**Finally, one additional question:  although I have my step count set to be from my watch exclusively with the app (all shows correctly!) since my phone is not tied to my hip the integration with Apple’s Health app only shows my phone’s step count.  Why does the app’s step count not utilize my choice of source when combined with the health app?  I use the Health app to integrate with rewards for healthy living from Walgreens & AARP.
Thank you!

***Nice quick response***
It is a rare instance where a developer offers a response so quickly!  Thank You!
Just to clarify, I already have my step count source set to my Gear Fit2 Pro.  (For anyone working off reviews, the developer’s response is an excellent demonstration how to do such if you do not know how to select!)
My steps always record from my watch, syncing each time I open my SHealth app.  My daily goal is always in my view, one way or another.
I guess what I am asking is, although my watch step count is correct in the SHealth app, why does my Apple Health app only show my phone’s step count (as opposed to my selected step count source properly recorded)?  Yes, they are linked with SHealth being a data source allowing Apple Health to read.  I have tried entering the difference in steps manually but it never saves. 
Thank you, again! 
STAY SAFE EVERYONE & PLEASE keep Social Distancing!

text:
When I first set up my CaringBridge account I was impressed and looking forward to using it. But it is no longer user-friendly.

If you look at other less-than-stellar reviews, you’ll notice that they’re not really reviews. They’re requests for help. The company replies to these by telling people to ask for help via their help page. 

Unfortunately, their help page is practically useless. It fails to answer the simplest questions. Using their chat feature is a waste of time, since it doesn’t understand the most basic questions. After a couple of tries, it says it is turning you over to a human. 

Alas, if you’re super unlucky, it tells you no humans are available, but they’ll contact you by email to help that way. That’s better than nothing, but by the time you’ve spent an hour struggling with the app, then struggling with the “help”, you might be pretty aggravated. 

That seems counterproductive for an app that’s supposed to make my life easier while I cope with a life-threatening illness.

Now that I’ve written all that, I’m lowering the rating from three stars to two. The only reason it’s not one star is because I’m holding onto hope that the app will become user friendly and helpful again.

Note to CaringBridge: If you respond to this by telling me to go to your help section, I’ll probably cry.

title: Helpful App - Sharing on iPad Not Working
text:
CaringBridge is a wonderful service and we appreciate it so much, especially in this time when our family has a member who has a life-changing medical condition. I offer this feedback as an opportunity for improvement and not a judgment.

When I share an update on my iPhone, the full action dialogue opens with all options available. On my iPad, I am presented with a tooltip and only the action dialogue header with the name of the app appears with no actions. I have looked to see if there is an option I have not enabled, but I can find none. I believe it may be a bug due to the tooltip container.

One other issue is that the app freezes in an auto-save mode which never resolves. I have to copy any content to the pasteboard or another app and force-quit. Once relaunched, there seems to be a window of time before it happens again. I paste the content and send before that happens usually. If I am interrupted, which can happen frequently for a caregiver, the issue reoccurs.

We are grateful for this app and this service. Thank you.

title: Review of CaringBridge
text:
I just had successful kidney transplant surgery at Mayo. 
I have had five years of FSGS, two and a half years of dialysis and three people trying to donate a kidney but being unable to due to health reasons. Literally hundreds of people have been praying for us, some I’ve never met!
Once we got the call and we were hustling to get from Greenville SC to Mayo in Minnesota ASAP the CaringBridge site provided the most effective and efficient way to communicate with anyone who desired information and updates. 
It has been a whirlwind week. My recovery is ahead of schedule and my doctors are all pleased. 
FIVE STARS AND THANK YOU CARINGBRIDGE!! ❤️😇🎯
Joel and Ann Shaw
Greenville SC
June 12, 2024

title: What happened?
text:
I’ve authored and co-authored several CaringBridge sites over the years. I have appreciated the relative ease of creating, updating and otherwise modifying sites - until earlier this year. Don’t know what happened to blow CaringBridge out of the water a few months ago, and the complete lack of communication about it was baffling. I’d still appreciate something more than “we’re working hard.”

While there’s been progress in recent months, the site still lacks much of its previous usability. As an author, I find it clumsy, difficult, and frustrating to use. More importantly, large numbers of my sister’s supporters and readers have stopped using it, and that is a very great loss.

Are there plans to restore more functionality? Will CaringBridge communicate anything of substance that might help its users? Is anyone paying attention to feedback from the community of users? I hope so.

Thanks for your time and attention.

text:
I bought this app years ago and never realized how useful at the time it was going to be for my future.
First my son had his phone stolen on the bus and I went directly to the house to retrieve it back in less than an hour. 

Second, my husband was in another state for work and experienced an accident. The phone didn’t notify me of anything regarding the accident, but when I couldn’t find him I was able to use the Life360 app to tell me where he was and the phone was located inside a hospital. He was brought in as unknown without identification and if it wasn’t for the app putting me in the correct direction it could have been weeks to months or not at all that I was notified about my husband’s whereabouts. Because of the app I was able to find him within a day of him arriving to the hospital and was able to get him started on surgeries he needed.

I’ve kept the app ever since and it’s very reassuring to have for regular day to day.

I would recommend it and I use it daily.

title: Delayed Safety Notifications Defeat the Purpose of Life360
text:
What good is Life360 for parents if notifications that our children have arrived at or departed from a location can be delayed by 3–5 minutes? Parents rely on this app for safety, awareness, and peace of mind. A notification that arrives several minutes after our child has already left or arrived defeats the purpose of receiving that alert in the first place.

When it comes to our children’s safety, timing matters. Parents should not have to wonder whether their child has left school, arrived home, or reached another destination while waiting several minutes for Life360 to notify them.

Life360 needs to take this issue seriously. Location and arrival/departure notifications should be delivered as promptly as technically possible, with reliable background tracking and minimal delays. If there is a technical limitation causing these delays, the company needs to explain it clearly and address it.

Parents depend on this app for more than convenience. We depend on it for information that helps us look after our children. A family safety app should prioritize timely, reliable notifications. Please fix this issue.

title: Doesn’t play well with digital displays
text:
I’ve subscribed to Cozi Gold since 2017 and love it, but will be cancelling my account. We have a digital display (Mango Display) and for months Cozi worked great. In February there was an update causing all day events to start at either 11pm the day prior or 4am day of. On very, very rare occasions it displays the start time correctly for a very short amount of time, we are talking a few minutes every few days/ weeks if that. I’ve watched the display flip start times between 11pm the day prior, 4 am day of and the correct all day time within seconds. I reached out to Cozi and their response was the calendar links port into Google Calendar correctly so it isn’t a problem on their end. That instead of selecting all day, time it from 0000 - 2359. Yeah, no. Mango Display cannot find the error on their part. I’ve tried other calendar links with Mango Display and all day events are displayed correctly leading to the belief that it is a Cozi issue. I give up since Cozi is unwilling to try and figure out the error to correct it. To me, it isn’t worth the price since it doesn’t perform how I need it to.


Editing after developer response : 
I initially agreed with your reply that it was a Mango Display issue until I found others using different digital displays that were having the same issue!  If you do a google search, you will find posts from users of other platforms that have their all day events over multiple days due to start time. 
A work-around was adding my cozi calendar to my Google Calendar and having that sync with Mango Display. All day events displayed correctly in both Google Calendar and on my Mango Display. This brings me back to why am I paying for something that doesn’t work how I need it to and I’m using a free option to achieve my goal.

That’s a major issue for an app that is solely focused on real time responsive checking and the information that’s on that list. It puts us in a really tough spot if we’re already out at the store and we’re having a ton of issues with the app because it requires my partner to give me a call and make sure that the things that I put on the list are actually on the list by choice and not buy a glitch. But I had to go to Reddit to figure out how to set a deficit because in the old app I could set my goal weight, current weight and the app would help me calculate my TDEE.  Now I have to use an outside TDEE calculator and the come back and set my calorie range.  Which is not clear at all and if I were just using the app I would assume by entering a goal weight it was giving me a correct calorie range. 

3.  AI slop - thankfully the app lets you turn off their AI coach so you don’t have to deal with that if you don’t want to. But I have to assume all of these changes are to force the user to use their AI and take pictures of their food to get calories and talk to their AI coach to get your true deficit so I find it high deceptive and gross.  Making a product worse isn’t changing people’s behavior to use it the way you want anymore - it’s just driving people away from the product.

title: Innacurate, and  downgrade from previous Fitbit app
text: I primarily use Fitbit for sleep tracking. My experience with the new app has been disappointing. The most notable problem with the app is its inaccuracy, but even the way data is presented is much less useful than offered in the original app. On my very first occasion using the app, after opening the old app and being required to download the new version I noticed that the total sleep reflected in the new app was 14 minutes higher than in the previous version of the app. The experience since that time has been similarly frustrating. For instance, I have come to learn that there are periods of time in which I have awakened before falling back asleep, and even periods of time in which I've gotten out of bed for several minutes before going back to bed and sleep, which are not reflected in the overall tracking of wakefulness over the course of a sleep session. For that reason total sleep time is, as previously mentioned, completely unreliable. Moreover, If the app isn't capable of measuring a change of state involving getting out of bed and walking around for 10 minutes before getting back into bed and going to sleep how can one rely on it making the far less certain discernment estimating a change in sleep from light to REM of deep, for example? I already had questions about Fitbit's accuracy when comparing it with an EEG measuring device I had previously used before that broke, but with the new Google Health app involved in the analysis I have it is clear that the way data is collected and measured is completely unreliable. Even the internal management and presentation of data is unacceptable. For instance, I have noticed that if I toggle between different detailed views for my daily sleep data in the app that the daily sleep score changes. Looking more closely I could see that other daily sleep metrics (such as total time asleep, and the length of different sleep stages) also changed, just by shifting views for a single, specific night. Beyond that problem the app can be confusing because it apparently defaults to weekly averages at times, so even when trying to navigate daily information one must sometimes reselect daily metrics after the app has inexplicably opted to switch back to weekly averages. So the experience of navigating data is very jumbled, with numbers bouncing all over the place, again even when limiting data elections exclusively to single, specific, daily measures. I'm also dissatisfied with the way that sleep tracking data set is presented. The level of detail and granularity is a downgrade from what was available on the previous Fitbit app. For instance, it used to be possible to see exactly how fractured sleep was broken down into periods of sleep and brief waking, but the new graphs make that impossible, only accounting for long periods of waking - periods of actual wakefulness are magically transformed into periods of sleep. At best, users of the new Google Health app will come away with only a vague sense of their sleep rather than the detailed analysis provided in the previous app. While I hope that this changes, I will immediately be looking for a new device from another company to take the place of my Fitbit because what Google provides now is not at all acceptable from a standpoint of accuracy and reliability.

title: The devs didn’t learn from their predecessors
text:
The app offers the basic features you’d expect from a health tracking app at a lower price point, with no subscription fees. That’s a solid selling point, but the execution needs work.

My biggest frustration is the lack of control over my own workout data. When the app overestimates my treadmill distance by a quarter mile, I should be able to correct it. Tracking errors happen. Preventing users from fixing them is a design choice—and a bad one. Guardrails are for rollercoasters, not my exercise log.

And why do I need Wi-Fi or cell service just to select a workout and start logging it? That’s basic functionality that should work offline, especially in an app people use while exercising.

For a Google app, this feels underwhelming. The price is appealing, but users need editable workout data, reliable offline functionality, and more control over their experience.

title: Great hardware held hostage by a brainless app
text:
I bought the $99 Fitbit Air to escape the wrist-screen doom-scroll. The tracker itself is actually great, but because it doesn't have a screen, you are entirely chained to the new Google Health app—and this app feels like it’s actively trying to sabotage my gains.

First, the UI is a joke. You can't just drag and drop widgets on your home screen. If you get the order wrong, you have to delete every single one and start over from the top like it's 2010.

Then there’s the built-in AI "coach." It confidently hallucinates food macros, and its understanding of exercise is purely comedic. It completely locks you out of making quick manual adjustments mid-workout. Want to log a Farmer's Walk or hit the sauna post-workout? The AI refuses to use a simple timer and forces you to log it as "sets and reps." Yes, let's all go crush 3 sets of 10 "sitting and sweating."

As an iPhone user, the experience is basically hostile. Google completely ignored iOS lock screen widgets, Live Activities, and even basic notification badges. If you want to check your rest timer or current set, you can't just glance at your phone. You have to pick it up with chalky, sweaty hands, pray Face ID recognizes your grimacing face, and manually open the app. Every. Single. Time.

But the ultimate sin is the mid-workout crash. The app randomly closed during a heavy session yesterday. When I reopened it, the AI cheerfully acknowledged I was in the middle of a mapped workout, but completely forgot all the weights, extra sets, and micro-adjustments I had just logged. I was forced to recreate my entire session from memory while oxygen-deprived.

Two stars because the screenless hardware is comfortable, but this software is currently more frustrating than a bench press plateau. Give it a pass until the engineers actually try working out with it.

title: Don’t think, just download it!
text:
This app has been a lifesaver for my family. Yes most of the features are things that come standard on any smartphone, however the convenience of having (almost) everything in one place has helped this busy Dad and Mom get more organized.

We downloaded this initially for the Recipe Box and Meal Planner tools (premium features). Add your favorite recipes to your recipe box, plan your meals, and it automatically adds the ingredients to your list. The amount of time we save each week on meal planning and grocery lists has been well worth the monthly fee!

There are a few features that are lacking and some I’d love to see incorporated.

99% of the time I use the app on my phone and when adding a new task or item to your list, it doesn’t allow you to categorize it until after you have submitted it, sending that to the “uncategorized” section at the bottom of the list. Being able to categorize it when you initially enter the data would save some clicks/time.

Another feature that could use an upgrade is the calendar. It’s nice being able to import your calendar, but integrating it so that you can create an event in the app and have it show up in your default calendar app would be a welcomed update. 

Add some iOS widgets (calendar, notes, todo, shopping list, etc.) 

A wishlist item would be Life360 integration or replacement. The maps is very basic and unreliable. We have noticed inaccuracy in the locations, delayed or non-existent notifications when leaving/arriving at one of our set places. Life360 is an excellent tool for not only location services, but also crash detection, driving summary, and more.

That being said. Don’t think, just download it!

title: Fantastic sanity saving app with one issue..
text:
I’d like to start by saying how much my family loves and appreciates this app.  I have OCD, so organization and planning is a huge part of my life.  I use FamilyWall every day, and it is DEFINITELY worth the premium price.  I mainly use the calendar, meal planner, recipe box, and lists. 

The calendar is fantastic because you can change the colors to better organize each event.  You can do recurring events.  I also love the layout of events and the way it shows the colored dots on the days that have something on the calendar. 

I love the recipe box and meal planner SO MUCH.  You can write in your own recipe, or make it a million times easier by using a link from a recipe online and FamilyWall enters it in for you.  It’s so helpful to have a list already there of our favorites and even some recipes we haven’t tried yet. 

I love the lists function too because, well, OCD and lists.  Lol.  

I have recently started using the budget function, and honestly, I was shocked to be disappointed with it.  There is a glitch showing that I’m way over budget even though I have entered in my income.  The income doesn’t show up unless you switch to a different week, then back to the week you’re working on.  Even then, it sometimes doesn’t fix it.  

I also don’t like that you can’t have separate spending limits for bills vs other expenses.  I would do away with the spending limit that covers all of the categories, and just stick with the page after that that allows you to enter in spending limits individually for each category.  I’d like to have some categories that don’t have a spending limit, but it restricts that because you have to have a limit for each category or it shows over budget.  It’s kind of redundant to have to budget the bills on the budget then have to do it again on spending limits because you already know your overall limit based on your income.  For me personally, I’d rather be able to separate bills and other categories because I don’t really have a choice on how much my bills are, so there’s no point in having a “limit” for how much they’ll be. 

My last issue is that there isn’t an option for money left from the week before to carry over into the next week, so you have to enter it as “income” the next week.  This, along with the other issues, is pretty frustrating because I do love this app so much, but I think I may have to find a different app for budgeting which also means talking my family into downloading yet another app.

I will say that the budgeting function has huge potential to be great.  I love that you can choose how often it reoccurs, and you can customize the days rather than just generic options like “daily, weekly, monthly”, etc.  It’s helpful to have that function because a lot of subscriptions come out every thirty days rather than every month on the same date.  I love that it calculates how much you have left to spend.  It gives me so much peace of mind knowing how much I actually have left to spend compared to looking at my bank account which always takes days for the payments to actually show.  I know exactly how much I have left to spend with this app!

Overall, I’m extremely happy with FamilyWall.  My only complaint would be with the budgeting function, and I’m looking forward to seeing improvements to it and adding another star back to my review.  Thank you for taking the time to create an app like this!  You guys are the reason my home runs smoothly and that I’ve remained sane!

Thank you for fixing the lockup with the “walking“ feature, which trapped users in an inescapable software backwater. Much appreciated. I have one other request: Can you please give us a choice to opt out of the app’s many functions that we don’t want?

Case in point: Please make it possible to remove references to MyFitnessPal, software that I used long ago, but not anymore, because it has been surpassed by its far more sophisticated rival, Cronometer. 

It would also be helpful if we could opt out of your questionably useful “Today’s Missions”, which are poorly executed and profoundly outdated, often focusing on studies that have been paid for by companies that can benefit from them. 

Some people might like these extras, but I find them completely useless and distracting. I value ability to control the powerful features of your hardware, but not at the expense of having to be distracted and annoyed by unnecessary fluff. 

Simply let users choose whether we’d like to use these extras or not. This is especially relevant because now, unlike before, you are forcing us to wade through lots of distractions just so we can utilize the sophisticated features of your hardware, for which we already paid a premium price.

text:
I wish I could give zero stars. The physical scale/watch is fine, but the iOS app is an absolute disaster that makes the entire ecosystem worthless. Withings has completely lost touch with its user base, prioritizing subscription revenue over basic functionality.
 
The Paywall is Anti-Consumer: It is infuriating to spend hundreds on a device, only to have core health metrics locked behind the "Withings+" subscription. Users on the r/withings forum have repeatedly pointed out that features like Vascular Age and Electrodermal Activity (EDA) are suddenly restricted unless you pay up, even though these were previously accessible or promised as part of the hardware purchase . It feels like a bait-and-switch.‌￼
 
FDA Approval Means Nothing Here: You mentioned the FDA approval—it's a joke in this context. Even though Withings touts its FDA-cleared ECG, the app experience is so broken that the data is useless. Furthermore, users have discovered that even with FDA clearance, Withings still puts up arbitrary barriers (like requiring a "prescription" for ECG in the US) while simultaneously failing to deliver on basic data syncing . The hardware might be medically approved, but the software is not fit for purpose.‌￼‌￼
 
The App is Broken and Ignored: The recent updates (like 5.13 and the 2025 releases) have destroyed the user experience. The timeline is gone, it's cluttered with useless notifications, and data often fails to load . Worse, the sleep tracking and HRV scores have become wildly inaccurate and inconsistent since recent updates, with scores fluctuating overnight without any physical change . Customer service just ignores the flood of complaints .‌￼‌￼‌￼
 
Don't Buy It: Until Withings stops treating its paying customers as beta testers and stops holding basic health data hostage behind a subscription, do not buy their products. Avoid this app.

Because it is outside the two-year warranty, the offer was 30% off a new scale, which now costs more than double what I paid. That is about $100 to replace a working product that Withings itself broke, with no reason to expect the next one would last any longer. title: They turned a bathroom scale into a subscription hostage situation
text:
Do NOT buy a Withings scale in 2026.

I bought Withings hardware to measure my weight, my body fat, my BMI and send it to Apple Health, where literally every other health device I own lives. That used to be the whole point of a smart scale.

As of October 13, 2026, Withings decided that basic feature is now a rent payment. Create a new Withings account today and you cannot export your own data to Apple Health or Health Connect unless you pay for Withings+ about $100/year. Not for coaching. Not for AI insights. Not for anything new. Just to move a number the scale you already paid for measured, from their app to Apple's app.

That's not a premium feature. That's a toll booth on your own data.

And don't let the "existing users are grandfathered" line fool you that's an admission, not a defense. They know current owners would revolt if they cut us off, so they're only screwing the next buyer who won't read the fine print until after setup, when they hit a paywall screen trying to turn on Apple Health sync. Your account gets deleted, you switch phones/emails, you set up a scale for your spouse/kid/parents? Welcome to the subscription.

This ruins the product. A smart scale that doesn't freely sync to Apple Health isn't smart, it's a walled garden with a glass platform. The hardware is now irrelevant I can't recommend a product whose business model is "buy the device, then pay us forever to actually use it in your health ecosystem."

Buy an InBody instead. The InBody Dial / H20N does proper 8-electrode body composition, syncs to the InBody app, and integrates with Apple Health, Google Fit, and Samsung Health with no subscription costs to access your body composition data. You buy it, you own it, it works. Revolutionary concept.

Withings used to be the easy recommendation. Now it's an easy warning: do not buy hardware from a company that will charge you rent to export your own weight.

This app lets me look at interactions and information about my medications if I want to.  I can change the time of a single or a group of meds just for one time or even skip one or all.  I can change the looks of the meds by shapes and colors so certain ones stand out.  I can delete meds and still keep the history of the med, or even just suspend the med.  This app really does it all.
I only have one complaint.  I wish more and different voices were periodically added.  I would pay a little extra for that because I have been listening to the same ones now for many years.  All-in-all, this is truly the best medication reminder app available (and I have tried them all!)

title: Such a bad user experience, it's potentially DANGEROUS.
text:
What an awful user experience. When setting up the meds, it turns out that 3x a day is NOT the same as "every 8 hours"—even though this is how hospitals do it. So it crams 3 doses into less time than intended, which is potentially dangerous. 

Next, the pill reminder is borderline unusable. There are 3 different views of your medications and schedule, and they each contain different information. The primary view doesn't even show my next dosing time. Why?

And if you take a dose late or early, it DOESN'T take that into account in your next dose (!!!!). So users, especially those who may have cognitive decline, can easily double up on dangerous meds like painkillers. 

This app is DANGEROUS, unusable, and embarrassingly bad. No clue how it has top ratings. Use Apple Health or write it down manually; don't risk your health.

It happened in March, and while I'm sure I had done it before, I redid my wife as emergency contact. And tested it to confirm the text message arrived. Just now I again found the computer said there wasn't an emergency contact and needed to set one up in the app. Checked and the app showed my wife with a verified phone number. I then verified her email and now the computer shows her verified and testing get assistance sends the phone text and email. And her phone shows the previous test from March. So I don't know when it broke, but at some point I lost that safety feature due to another Garmin bug. 

Feature bugs are one thing, but this is a safety bug. At least she would have my live track, which has never broken, but I hate that I bought a computer for a safety system that is too buggy to trust. text:
Garmin Connect provides excellent fitness data, advanced metrics, and workout functionality, but the music/download experience desperately needs improvement.

Managing downloaded playlists and music on a Forerunner 265 is unnecessarily difficult. There should be a simple option in Garmin Connect to view what music is currently downloaded to the watch, add or remove playlists, and force a music refresh directly from the phone. title: “Lively Mobile +” with Fall Detection ✅
text:
Only three days after receiving my “Lively Mobile+” medical alert device, I bent over to pick up something small I had stepped on in my bare feet. 
The next thing I knew, I had crumpled and was sitting upright, on the floor, blankly looking around. (I’ve had a degenerative muscle condition for 30 years). 
I had began thinking “Well, That was unexpected!”
Then I heard a pleasant, confident voice greeting me by name… from my device:
“Mrs. Pearson your device indicates you had a fall. Are you alright?” Or something similar to that. She also asked several questions checking in my condition. Did I hit my head?, was I injured? etc. Which were all great because a hard fall can leave me befuddled a bit at first. 
Next she asked permission to put me on hold while she called Emergency Services and for me to please stay on the line. 
She was soon back to me and waited with me until Emergency Services showed up. The the call was pleasantly ended. 
Sign me: A Happy, Protected Customer
————
Note - the device runs on a full charge for approximately 80 hours. 
If it runs low, an unusual beep sounds … Even at 2:30 in the morning. 
I have decided mark Charging Days on my calendar until it is a habit. 
————
Special Note - I expected the device to be annoying to wear. I think I even wanted to hate it because it represented another stage of becoming more disabled. 
I was 100% wrong. 
Instead of being annoying, it is comfortable and I was surprised with how quickly I became adjusted to wearing it all the time. 
Favorite Detail about the “Lively Mobile+” model - My particular medical insurance paid for the device and all the monthly fees. 
If you’re considering this device, at least give your insurance company a call and see if it is covered or helpful on the costs. 
Since I live alone, my family and other loved ones are glad I took this step forward towards safety. They also like the free “Lively Link” app (shows clasped hands on the icon) where they can find out if I’ve had falls or been out and about. The GPS feature helps with that.

When I reload the app 5 minutes later, the updated location is available. I don't know why it takes time. Maybe it's a batch operation running on a mainframe computer. We get piece of mind from this app, in spite of the fact that results aren't instantly available. The service that answers calls seems terrific. We are very satisfied. If you seek software perfection, you may need to keep looking. This isn't self-contained technology like some game on your phone. You're trying to track down an inexpensive cellular device that may be roaming between cell towers. This one isn't perfect but it does the job and the app costs nothing.

title: Inconsistent coverage
text:

Again I logged out n then turned off my phone for a few minutes and then went through the process of turning my phone back on and logging in again.  It now shows that the device is on and the battery is charging. My friend is diligent about wearing the device and charging it nightly.  If I can not get consistent and accurate information from my link that is a problem.  Also, it is concerning that technical support is not available 24/7. If this device is meant to aid the elderly or persons with medical issues technical support should be available or at least have a tech person on call that can handle any incoming request for assistance.  This is my 1st experience with Great Call and it's device.  At this time I am frustrated with the inconsistency and the lack of tech staff to assist outside of regular  customer service hours.  I hope improvements will be made.

Frustrated caregiver

title: Great Call to Unreliable Call
text: Has gone from excellent to TRASH. Have been a very happy user for FOUR YEARS until lately. Am still researching, talking with tech support, and am actually riding around to field test problems. We used to get 95%+ success in locating wearer. Now we get maybe 10% success. Same house. Same car. Same town. Same frequent destinations. Small town. No new developments. There is a Verizon tower about 2 and 1/2 miles from house. It appears the issue is that the Lively Mobile device is 3G technology and what Verizon tells me is it gets lowest priority on 4G towers so it will be slower and slower to update and may get shut out entirely during more busy times. That explains why sometimes ( rarely now) it succeeds in seconds and other times ( more frequently) it tries forever and still fails. As more towers convert to 4G these other reviewers that are singing it's praises as I once did will be left behind as well.  As per just the app, it too is flawed. The info it gives you does NOT really mean what it says. It could be HOURS old yet it tells you wearer was at a location, say, 10 minutes ago. It simply IGNORES all the failed attempts. There is more; that's just one example. I may update after field test. System is failing. App doesn't account for failure thus making it inaccurate.

title: Does not work
text: I had an app on the old device that did not have fall protection and it worked fine. The new app for the fall protection device doesn't work at all no matter how many times I've contacted the company they still can't make it work.

title: Unreliable
text: Not very reliable.  Move device from one room to another and tells all I am out.  Needs a lot of work.  Also takes too long to update location.

title: Great idea; poor functionality
text: GPS very often does not work at all. When it does work updates are in frequent. For example, it tells me my mom was out and about 2 1/2 hours ago. That's a long time to go without an update! The Help staff usually does try to be helpful; I just think the system needs a lot of improvement.

title: Not impressed
text:
Bought great call Splash with ultimate plan for my mother and Aunt.  Tested the devices and response time was under 10 seconds.  Great. Charge lasted several days. Good. Then I turned on fall protection.  When fall protection was turned on the battery life significantly decreased.  I have to recharge it after about 13-15 hours. Not good, and the rep told me that was standard for fall protection. I will have to turn off auto fall protection to keep the device on my moms neck and off of the cradle. The Great Call Link app is UNRELIABLE. It always shows battery charging, even when it's not on the charger.  The device status ALWAYS displays ON even when I've turned it off for the better part of the day.  The GPS seems to be working fine for the most part. The ability to check the device ALWAYS returns a server error.  I wish I could rely on this app but I can't.

Update:  The battery display appears to be working. Other than the GPS nothing else is working. My mom pressed the button. I thought I would get notified. Instead, that event became a tiny note in the app.  Summaries appear in reverse chronological order. I would not recommend paying extra for this app. The latest version did nothing to fix prior issues.

title: CRO
text: App completely untrustworthy worked one day. Then would close as soon as screen tried to refresh without showing any info. Ran the latest update now it won't show anything but the sign on screen and the company info block. Can't access any tracking info at all.

title: Not reliable
text: When this app works, it does a great job of tracking the phone user, and the mapping is accurate. Lately, it has been unable to locate the user or tells me the device is not on. This, even when I'm TALKING to the user on the land line, and she's confirming that her cell phone is on and charged. May be a network problem on Great Calls side, but since the main reason I got the Jitterbug phone for my 88 year old mom was to be able to track her, these outages are completely unacceptable.

title: Both frustrated user and bad experience user names were taken, how bad could it be?
text: Like a lot of customers have complained already - it only works for a few days, then everything stopped working. The 5*, the GPS, the battery indication, the greatcall link app, and, the customer service. They don't know the basics and they gave an impression that the Estimated fix time is just beyond your grace period. How can one rely on this for a life saving aid device for the elder-lies?

title: Love it
text: Love that I can keep track of my aunt. Also… knowing The devices charged and being used and is on perfect also love knowing when she's leaving the house and returns gives me peace of mind.

title: iPhone / iPad
text: Worked great for 2 years. Now it works on my iPad but not much on my iPhone 6. Keeps telling the unit is off or trouble connecting to server on iPhone but works fine on iPad.

title: Works now
text:
It seems as though, after I wrote a poor review
out of frustration, the app seems to work. So I added 2 stars to my original review. This is great as long as it works.

title: Needs an overhaul.
text:
Update- The app has not updated its status (battery level, locations, weekly reports, 5 star call info, etc.) since May 12th. It's now June 9th. 

The concept for the app is great. The functionality is lacking. You can't track more than one account (though that issue to me is bigger than the app since you can't have more than one person on an account). The locations are a bit buggy (the app likes to notify me often that my mother is in random places between 4-5am when I see that she's in bed asleep any time she actually leaves the home it tells me nothing). It is constantly showing that the device is charging even when she's wearing it. Rarely does it notify me that she's out and about; in fact most of the notifications never show up (except for those random places at 4-5 in the morning). It's slow; everything you try to do on the app is slow no matter your phone or connection. For the most part, I feel that it needs to be more functional. After all, more times than not the people using the app are not the ones wearing the devices/using the phones so it doesn't need to simplified so much that nothing works and what does work has little to no options for use.

title: App crashes
text: Loaded app in IPhone 6 - sign in and app crashes - link support has not been able to help. One month - worthless if not able to track

title: GPS Stinks
text: Although I love the concept, in reality the GPS stinks! My 85 yr old mother has the splash. The app's GPS shows my mother being out and about all through the middle of the night when she's home in bed sleeping. This can be extremely frightening to loved ones. I've gotten Calls at 3am from concerned siblings!! Need to fix thi!

title: Unreliable
text: I had high hopes for this app, but as others have stated, it needs a major overhaul. Unreliable, says it's charging when it's around my mom's neck, says she's out and about the day AFTER she was actually out and about, weekly update doesn't update - I could go on and on. Being able to have all of her medications, dosages etc at hand is a feature plus, but using the app to keep up with my mom is useless.

title: Quit Working
text: This app worked the first few months but then stopped tracking. More often than not, the app shows the phone is off or not in service when, in fact, it is on and fully charged.

title: Limited tracking
text: We bought this phone, not for an elder parent, but for our 13-year old son to use as his communication device when we need to take away his iPhone for disciplinary reasons.  For that purpose, it's fine. (It's actually a very humiliating phone for a teenager to carry around!)  But it does not offer the kind of real-time whereabouts information that the iPhone provides.  The "Jitterbug" only seems to ping the location server every 20 minutes or so.  When you need to know where your kid is right now, a message like "About 15 minutes ago Junior was out and about" is quite frustrating.

title: False Battery indicator and GPS function not working on Great Call Link
text: Software unstable. Great Call has a problem with reporting the correct battery state. It also says the phone is offline and it is not. It is online with a good signal.

title: Forget it
text: I bought this device with high hope that it would solve a problem with a 91 year old live alone dad out in the boonies. I was happy with it for the first few days then it went to crap. The app now shows the Splash is always in the charger, it always shows the power is on even when turned off for 30 minutes. For the last few days it always shows he is at home when I know he is not. I've been in touch with tech support many times.  The standard answer is turn it off turn it on maybe it will work by tomorrow.  Or better yet, "are you at home?  The device says your at home so that's ok." That's all it ever says these days.

title: App doesn't show location
text: Since I bought the phone for my father, the app doesn't show where he is. It always gives me an error saying that the device is not activated or 5star are having issues. It's been 2 weeks since and they still have not fixed it. This is the only reason I got this phone for my father. Really disappointed. Customer service keeps telling me it will take a couple of days to fix the issue and still not working 2 weeks later.

title: Inconsistent
text: For something this important the app gives false readings on battery life and on/off line.  It also indicates my Mom is Out and About often miles away when she hasn't moved outside her very small house.. In addition it indicates she hasn't used the fob for several days as if that's a bad thing.  When we press the button the app ultimately wakes up but it is unnerving.  We will have to look for more secure solutions.

title: Love My GreatLink
text: I was a bit hesitant to get the "GreatCall Splash" because I am JUST under 50. However, due to my medical conditions I am in dire need of something so my husband and daughter know I'm safe. My daughter loves that she gets notifications letting her know where I am! I haven't had ANY negative issues that I know of. The only problem I have is I clip the unit to my purse, and if I place it down carelessly, it thinks there's been a "Fall Detected" and I have to press the button right away to interrupt the call. It happens A LOT.

title: Peace of Mind
text:
This app gave my Mother such peace of mind.  Knowing that I know where she is at any moment, when she leaves home and keeps me updated continuously.

I wanted this for my benefit because of the GPS tracking and the falling feature-  and when she agreed I was thrilled. We both feel relief and peace of mind.

title: Keeping mom safe - Splash + Great Call service
text:
I live in a different state and use the system as a safeguard to ensure my 89 year old mother is safe at home. I primarily use the app to locate her and it works well in Phoenix. I can distinguish between her being in the backyard or in the house, or any other location she chooses to travel to in the area. It helps balance her independence and safety. 
I highly recommend Great Call service and the app for aging parents. The single button system is easy to use in an emergency or if she simply isn't feeling well. Thwy have her history and all relevant contact info. They know to call me if she has asked for help.

title: Not as good as some locators
text: The device does not update as quickly as a newer generation smart phone and either the device or the app result in showing a wrong location. When she is at home, the app shows her several hundred feet from her condo. If this were a single family home in a residential neighborhood, I would not worry so much but when it is a multi storied multi condo unit, I would worry that any first responders would be  misled. Last Sunday when she was in church, the app showed her on the fairway of one of the holes of a nearby golf course. I got a kick out of that! Bottom line, get Grandma an iPhone with "Find My Friends"

title: GreatCall no link
text: I have yet to be able to connect to the phone to utilize any of the functions listed :(. Very, very disappointed to always see "no status"

title: Very pleased.
text: My mother bought this for my father who had a few falls.  They are happier knowing that if something happens someone is there to get them help.  I feel less anxious being able to get updates with the app.

title: Fulfills the Purpose

But the weekly updates are not kept in reverse chronological order and if there is a problem between the device and the App, I've always had to delete the App (and all the data) to correct the problem.  I don't think there is a better system out there; I really don't.  I just wish the data they collect through the GPS would be more thorough.

title: Frustrating App!
text: This app is driving me crazy!  Very disappointed. It works sporadically and it's very unreliable. I live over 400 miles away from my 91 year old mother, and was hoping this app would provide me with some level of comfort in keeping connected to her when I'm not physically talking to her on the phone. It initially worked well, but shortly after started giving inaccurate information. It would indicate that my mother left home at 1:15 a.m. and returned at 1:45 a.m.  My mother lives alone and doesn't drive. Now I'm getting a message that says the device is turned off or not in service.  I've called support and I'm told the app is rarely wrong. The concept behind this app is great so I hope they find a way to fix these issues. I sure hope her actual device is functioning far more accurately than the smart phone app!

title: Disappointing GPS
text:
I looked forward to being able to know when my mom was out and about and then safely home but the GPS function is terrible.  Inaccurate location info.  Others have noted the delay in updates, which I am willing to allow for in order to limit the battery drain. But the lack of accuracy is not acceptable. The app has said mom has traveled a mile or more from home when she had not left the house all day. And other times it did not record a trip she did take. Very disappointed in this functionality.   

It does seem to be accurate on the battery level, however. I'm hoping they will work on the other issues as this app could be extremely useful to family members and other caregivers.

text: I am using this App and website while I’m going through brain surgery. Another favorite is the progress charts. They let me see at a glance if I have taken my schedules medications and how much as needed pain and nausea medication I have taken. 

The reports let me give my physician a PDF as needed. And makes it much easier for us to discuss treatment regiments especially in conjunction with the symptoms tracker. 

Support team is also available and responsive within 24 hours. 
Thank you to the App makers for producing and maintaining this critical app. It has been a gamechanger as my disease progresses and helps relieve anxiety over medication and keeps me on track.

title: Don’t record before reading this
text:
This app may collect audio recordings and transcripts of private medical appointments, and those conversations may be processed by third-party API providers. Before pressing record, users should know exactly where their doctor-patient conversation goes, what is retained, what is deleted, and how this free, venture-backed app plans to make money.

Kin’s privacy materials raise serious questions. Does Kin delete the original audio after transcription? How long are transcripts, summaries, and backups retained? What exact data does Kin keep after each visit? Can Kin use deidentified or aggregated medical conversation data to improve products, analytics, or future models? Can that data ever be shared, transferred, licensed, sold, or used commercially? What happens to user data if Kin is acquired?

Saying third-party providers are restricted from training general-purpose AI models on user data does not answer these core questions. Doctor visits can include diagnoses, prescriptions, mental health, reproductive health, family history, insurance issues, and other deeply personal information.

The privacy disclosure should be impossible to miss before recording begins: whether the audio leaves the phone, whether outside API providers process it, what is stored, what is deleted, how long data is retained, and what rights Kin claims over deidentified or aggregated health data.

Until those answers are clear, users should be very cautious about recording doctor visits with Kin.

text:
워낙 깜빡해서 차라리 달력을 상대방과  공유할 수 있으면 좋겠다 생각하던 차에 이 어플을 발견했습니다. 
어느날 캘린더가 갑자기 리셋되어 다른 일정이 뭐였는지 다시 정리하느라 고생한 적이 있습니다. 이참에 연인끼리 캘린더를 공유해서 서로 일정도 알고 챙겨주자해서 같이 시작했습니다. 평소 일정을 물어보지 않아도 캘린더 등록 알람으로 상대방 일정이 추가된 것을 실시간으로 알 수 있고, 까먹으면 캘린더 들어가서 확인할 수도 있었습니다. 
연인끼리 서로 가능한 날짜를 한눈에 볼 수 있어 데이트날짜 정하기 편하고, 간단하게 서로의 일정을 알 수 있어 이전대화내역 뒤져보는 귀찮음도 없고 불안하지도 않습니다. 
사용하다보니 연인뿐만 아니라 각종 모임에서도 매우 유용할 것 같습니다. 
저는 운동, 개인 목표달성과 관련된 캘린더를 추가로 만들어 사용하고 있습니다. 연인/러닝모임/달성기록 등 각각의 캘린더를 동시에 겹쳐서 한눈에 볼 수도 있고, 원하는 캘린더만 지정해서 볼 수도 있습니다.

We use the calendar for our appointments, meetings, trainings, important events, outreach, classes, and Holidays. title: Completely useless with iPhones/iOS
text:
I replaced my FitBit with a Fossil smart watch, and WearOS + Google Fit have been absolute garbage. I should explain that I bought this watch because I love Fossil’s products, but before I even bought it I double-checked to be sure Wear OS would work with iPhones. It claimed that it does (this is a lie), so I felt comfortable with my purchase at the time. Since then, Wear OS and Google Fit have been nothing but a complete disappointment. Fit will not record steps either on my watch or my phone, even after doing a factory reset (this seems to be a common problem regardless of the platform if the Wear OS help forum is any indication). There are a ton of features in Wear OS that are Android-compatible only. I can’t get texts or calls on my watch. The moon phase and sunrise/sunset option don’t work unless it’s connected to a network, which is completely stupid since those are based on time and date, which are already in the watch to begin with. I would think they should maybe only have to sync once a week to keep accurate. Both Wear OS and Fit are aggravatingly limited in their functions: Fit is stupidly basic and doesn’t have things like nutrition or period tracking. Wear OS doesn’t give you any options to alter watch settings through the app, except to change the watch face, which you can also do on the watch, so really, why bother? Long story short, I have a really fancy watch that doesn’t work at all for any of the purposes I bought it for, but hey, it looks cool. I’m going back to my FitBit for health tracking.

Google, fix your s**t. This is unacceptable.
